instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Energy services company providing energy efficiency audits, HVAC optimization, and building management system integration for commercial and industrial clients. Completed 200+ projects across hospitals, hotels, and manufacturing plants. Developing an IoT-based real-time energy monitoring platform.
answers.pastInitiatives: We have a mature innovation program with a dedicated R&D lab of 12 engineers, an annual innovation budget equivalent to 5% of revenue, and a structured stage-gate process for evaluating and funding new initiatives. In the past 3 years we have launched 4 new product lines that now contribute 18% of total revenue, including an AI-powered recommendation engine that has become our fastest-growing SKU.
answers.strategicGoals: The board has challenged us to improve EBITDA margins by 500 basis points within 3 years. This requires a disciplined, data-driven approach to identifying cost drivers and process bottlenecks. We are open to technology investment if it demonstrably reduces unit costs or eliminates manual touchpoints, but every project must have a clear ROI timeline of under 12 months.
answers.additionalContext: We completed a merger with a similarly-sized competitor 4 months ago and are in the middle of integrating teams, systems, and processes. The combined organization has significant duplication — two CRMs, two HR systems, overlapping product lines. There is a unique window to redesign processes from scratch rather than patching legacy approaches, but cultural integration is fragile and change fatigue is real.
answers.teamSize: Our R&D function consists of 10-12 engineers organized into two squads: one focused on core product innovation and one on exploratory/new business model prototyping. We also have 2 dedicated data engineers building our analytics infrastructure. Innovation projects follow a lean startup methodology with clear go/no-go criteria at 3-month checkpoints.

opportunities.title: Smart Contract Integration for Energy Audit Reporting
opportunities.rationale: Given the formal process and focus on efficiency, implementing smart contracts to automate invoicing and validation of energy audit compliance can drastically reduce manual administrative touchpoints. This is a low-risk way to drive operational excellence.

first_actions: Identify current reporting bottlenecks in the ERP/CRM flow.
Pilot smart contract integration on one specific, high-volume service line (e.g., HVAC optimization).
Define key performance indicators (KPIs) for reduction in administrative hours.
resources_needed: Contractor specialist for blockchain/smart contract auditing.
2 dedicated data engineers for system integration mapping.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduce project overhead cost by 15% within the first quarter of pilot.
milestones: Week 4: Finalize scope and technical feasibility.

opportunities.title: Automated Data Cleanup and Integration Workflow
opportunities.rationale: The post-merger environment presents a major opportunity to streamline data flow. Developing an automated workflow for cleaning duplicate customer records and consolidating disparate CRM/HRIS data will improve the efficiency of sales and service operations without requiring new technology development.

first_actions: Map current data silos between legacy systems.
Develop a Python-based ETL script focused solely on deduplication.
Establish governance rules for master data management.
resources_needed: 1 full-time Data Engineer dedicated to integration.
Internal process documentation team time allocation.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in manual reconciliation time by 25% across sales and service teams.
milestones: Month 1: Complete system mapping and data flow audit.
Month 3: Automated workflow for cleaning implemented and tested.

opportunities.title: Predictive Maintenance Model for Utility Infrastructure
opportunities.rationale: A bold shift involves leveraging the newly developed IoT monitoring platform to create a predictive maintenance model that forecasts equipment failure before it occurs. This moves beyond reactive auditing into proactive, data-driven cost avoidance, directly supporting the strategic goal of margin improvement.

first_actions: Select one high-risk physical asset class (e.g., industrial pumps/transformers).
Gather historical operational data and sensor telemetry.
Train machine learning models using current R&D talent.
resources_needed: 1 Senior ML Engineer dedicated to model development.
Hardware sensor deployment budget ($50k initial capital expenditure).
execution_plan.success_metric: Achieve 80% accuracy in predicting equipment failure within a 30-day window.
milestones: Month 1: Data pipeline established and cleaned.
Month 6: Initial model training complete and validated against historical data.
Month 9: Pilot deployment on 5 key assets.

next_steps.action: Establish a cross-functional Efficiency Task Force to formally define the top 3 process bottlenecks identified during the merger.
Allocate $50k from the innovation budget for a proof-of-concept focused on reducing manual data entry using low-code automation tools.
Conduct a talent gap analysis focusing specifically on predictive analytics skills to address the key barrier of 'talent'.

key_weaknesses: Fragmented legacy systems leading to significant data duplication and integration challenges post-merger.
Limited budget (5% of revenue) constrains the ability to pursue large, long-term infrastructure projects.
High sensitivity to cultural change fatigue hindering the adoption of new processes across integrated teams.
Potential talent gap in advanced predictive analytics required for achieving aggressive margin goals.
